quoted.author: Ben Casnocha
quoted.text:
People in mid-life, mid-career don't usually have a singular "crisis" moment, despite the mid-life crisis namesake.

Rather, the mid-life crisis shows up as "a slow ebb into a quiet and often befuddling restlessness and dissatisfaction."

(via Nathan Hill)

items.author: J.K. Lundblad | Teaching Progress
items.text:
Lunar landing denial is a special kind of stupid.

I'll admit, as a young kid, I was intrigued by the notion that NASA faked the landings.

We hadn't been back to the Moon in decades. Which does seems odd, doesn't it? Humans went to the Moon, only to be unable to return.....??

Nephew who HATES sweet potatoes gave it 10/10. If you're not diabetic, it's worth a try.

quoted.author: Math Pulse
quoted.text:
A town where everyone uses “word A” for something, say what to call a street. Now add a few people who use “word B” and never change, whatever anyone says.

Does the town change its word?

With 5% stubborn people, word B ends at only 6%. With 16%, it reaches 100%. Repeated runs put the tipping point near 10%, and the closer the stubborn share is to it, the longer the crowd takes to decide.

This is the naming game, studied by physicists and linguists as a model of how conventions form.

The surprise is how small the minority can be: nobody has to be persuaded by argument. They only have to be certain, and let everyone else's habits do the rest.

coverage: Eight posts, November 2026. Compiled Wednesday, Nov. 25, ET.
